Alright, what a couple of days it’s been. Grab your coffee, here’s the rundown from your favorite news-junkie pal.

***

### Money Talk

- **Jensen Huang’s wild ride back to Nvidia CEO sends stocks soaring.**
  The chip giant reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after allegations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, with President Trump reportedly personally ensuring his comeback. Nvidia's stock surged, adding nearly $1 trillion to its market value and setting options-trading records. Apparently, some people are just "too big to fail." [S1][S4][S5][S7][S9][S10][S11][S13][S19][S53][S71]
- **Trump’s Nvidia intervention raises eyebrows, fuels "too big to fail" debate.**
  President Trump's direct involvement in Huang's reinstatement is drawing bipartisan backlash on Capitol Hill, with critics calling it "troubling and problematic" and a national security headache. Allies, however, argued Huang was "too big to fail" for the U.S. economy, painting him as a victim of "deep state" maneuvering. [S17][S18][S19][S26][S36][S50]
- **CrowdStrike's $44B Zscaler bet defended by CEO.**
  CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz is out defending the company's hefty $44 billion acquisition of Zscaler, calling it a "winning combination." Let's see if that synergy holds up or if it’s just a big-ticket gamble. [S2]
- **AI adoption gains traction in Asia, but metrics remain fuzzy.**
  Businesses across Asia-Pacific are increasingly investing in AI and seeing some returns, according to an AWS survey. The catch? Many are still struggling to accurately measure those gains, meaning the ROI narrative might be more vibes than hard data for now. [S3]
- **Retailer Next hit by supplier cyber-attack, warns customers.**
  Fashion and homewares giant Next issued a cyber-attack warning after hackers accessed data through a third-party technology supplier. While they believe no personal data leading to fraud was compromised, it's another reminder that your supply chain is only as strong as its weakest link. [S15]

### World Lore

- **Russia’s war in Ukraine keeps spilling over, now hitting NATO borders.**
  NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte is doing damage control after three Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland, not to mention a Ukrainian attack sinking a Russian warship in Libya and new allegations of Russian ops in Denmark. The "special military operation" seems increasingly uncontained. [S21][S23][S24]
- **COP31 climate talks crater, ending in record-long deadlock.**
  The 31st climate change conference ran two days longer than expected, making it the longest summit in history, only to conclude with absolutely no deal. Great work, everyone. More hot air than actual progress. [S22]
- **Trump blacklists Megaspeed, escalating fallout from Nvidia saga.**
  The Trump administration just added Megaspeed, a company linked to the Nvidia scandal, to a trade blacklist. This move came on the same day Jensen Huang was reinstated, adding another layer of geopolitical drama to the tech CEO’s contentious comeback. [S31][S45]
- **Jared Kushner's Albanian real estate plans hit a local snag.**
  A company working for Jared Kushner dropped $130 million on 300 acres in Albania, but local Albanians are saying "hold up, that’s *our* land." Expect some interesting property disputes with international flavor. [S25]
- **Denmark’s top court backs controversial "ghetto law" evictions.**
  Denmark's Supreme Court upheld the country’s "ghetto law," ruling that evictions of "non-Western" residents do not constitute discrimination. Copenhagen argues the law promotes integration, while critics point to blatant ethnic profiling. [S32]

### Tech Tea

- **Nvidia's Jensen Huang is back, sparking celebration and scandal.**
  The tech world is still buzzing (and divided) over Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO. Elon Musk cheered the "corrected mistake," while critics hammered Trump's intervention as a major national security risk. It's truly peak 2026. [S4][S7][S9][S10][S11][S13][S17][S18][S19][S26][S27][S36][S44][S45][S50][S51][S53][S54]
- **Anthropic's Claude Ship lets AI agents review and approve code.**
  As AI-generated code floods dev pipelines, Anthropic is launching Claude Ship, a new suite of tools that lets AI agents handle routine code change approvals. The bots are now managing the bots – what could possibly go wrong? [S42]
- **Kagi takes on Gmail with a privacy-first email service.**
  The Google alternative Kagi, already offering paid search and a Chrome rival, just launched Kagi Mail. Their promise: "no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in." A noble effort, but trying to unseat Gmail is like fighting a hydra. [S46]
- **GTA VI leaker sentenced but walks free due to time served.**
  Arion Kurtaj, the hacker behind the massive Grand Theft Auto VI leaks, was sentenced to seven years in prison but immediately released on license. Apparently, hacking Rockstar Games and others only gets you a slap on the wrist these days. [S47]
- **Nvidia pushes into brain-computer interfaces with Paradromics.**
  Beyond AI chips, Nvidia is now powering brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) through a partnership with Paradromics. They'll be processing direct brain data. Just when you thought tech couldn’t get any more mind-bending. [S55]

### Creator Szn

- **Advertisers wrestle with "agentic media" in the AI era.**
  The ad world is trying to figure out "agentic media," building AI systems around existing human teams, data, and rules. It’s all about creating specialized AI agents, but the real test is whether they actually deliver better results or just more buzzwords. [S56]
- **Ad agencies' AI hype clashes with clients' demand for results.**
  Agencies spent the last two years selling AI as an efficiency play, promising leaner teams and lower fees. Clients, however, are now asking why invoices haven't shrunk, hinting at a growing chasm between AI promises and actual, measurable outcomes. [S57]
- **Holiday marketing goes all-in on CTV and streaming.**
  This holiday season, brands are shifting their marketing budgets, with CTV and streaming ads gaining serious traction over traditional TV. It’s a clear sign that eyeballs are moving, and advertisers are following suit, chasing those precious digital impressions. [S58]
- **Massive CTV ad fraud scheme "BADBOX 3.0" exposed.**
  HUMAN Security just unveiled "BADBOX 3.0," a CTV ad fraud scheme generating a staggering 40 billion bid requests a day. It’s a stark reminder that as digital ad spending grows, so does the sophistication of the fraudsters trying to siphon it off. [S59]
- **Gap Inc. leans into "fashiontainment" with boy bands and microseries.**
  Gap Inc. is betting big on "fashiontainment," partnering with boy band Just Your Type (JYT) and launching a scripted microseries for Banana Republic called "The Agency." Because apparently, selling clothes now requires a full-blown media empire. [S60]

### Supply Lines

- **UPS snags Smartways Logistics in acquisition play.**
  UPS is expanding its footprint by acquiring Smartways Logistics, a strategic move likely to boost its end-to-end supply chain capabilities as peak season kicks into high gear. [S76]
- **Amazon's drone delivery program has a minor fender bender.**
  An Amazon Prime Air delivery drone crashed into a garage in Huntington Woods, Michigan, just as the company was celebrating its drone launch in Mount Juliet, Tennessee. Guess even advanced tech has its bad days. [S83][S84][S85][S86]
- **DHL Supply Chain sees double-digit growth, eyes Philippines for expansion.**
  DHL's supply chain division reported a solid 12% revenue growth in Q3 2026, signaling strong performance, with the company specifically banking on continued expansion in the Philippines to fuel future gains. [S77][S78][S79]
- **Savannah port roars with 25% jump in October container traffic.**
  The Port of Savannah saw a massive 25% year-over-year increase in container traffic in October, handling over half a million TEUs, driven by robust import demand and ongoing infrastructure investments. That’s a lot of stuff heading our way. [S64]
- **Belgian air traffic strike snarls Black Friday cargo ahead of schedule.**
  Just days before Black Friday, a Belgian air traffic control strike has forced airlines to reroute flights and aircraft, disrupting cargo operations at key hubs like Liège and Brussels. Expect some potential delivery headaches. [S74]

### Speed Round

- Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, courtesy of Trump, added $1 trillion to its value.
- The GTA VI hacker got a seven-year sentence but was released immediately.
- COP31 went down in flames, becoming the longest, most unproductive climate summit ever.
- An Amazon delivery drone decided to redecorate a Michigan resident's garage.
- Turns out, paying someone £250 a month for "life admin" is a thing for busy moms.
- Russia’s war in Ukraine just flung more missiles into NATO territory, because why not?
- Gap Inc. is now doing "fashiontainment" with boy bands, because brands need to be *everywhere*.
